Texans are tired, Peter, and I am too.
We’re tired of Greg Abbott. Tired of the corruption. Tired of the chaos. Tired of watching our schools, health care, and basic affordability lose priority while he plays political games just to stay in power.
That’s why I’m running for Governor — because I’m determined to deliver for Texans.
**[If you’re with me, will you pitch in $5 today to help us keep the momentum going and beat Abbott in November?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260109_1_running.kHjqKJ&refcode=em20260109-388&amount=5&t=1&akid=388%2E299639%2EDDK0v3)**
Greg Abbott has had over a decade to prove he’s on our side — and he’s chosen who he works for. He’s built a government that rewards special interests and billionaire donors, while working families pay the price. And that price is everywhere.
* Public schools are closing
* Health care costs are rising while Texas ranks near the bottom
* Property taxes are still high
* Communities are struggling to afford the basics

An amazing state full of promise is being held back by a governor _obsessed_ with power.
Texas deserves leadership that’s focused on results. Leadership that believes government should make life easier for working families, not harder.

name: Senator Mark Kelly
subject: Join me for an exclusive conversation
body:
You’re invited to a conversation with Senator Mark Kelly
---
Hi Derek, Senator Mark Kelly here. I’m excited to share that I will be hosting an exclusive conversation alongside the DNC Grassroots Team on **Wednesday, January 21, at 6 PM ET.** President Trump and his Defense Secretary, Pete Hegseth, have now taken the extra step of formally censuring me. Just earlier this week, the DOD launched a process to demote me in retirement and cut my pension, all because they didn’t like what my colleagues and I said in a video reminding members of the military of our laws and the oath we all took to our Constitution. They’ll never understand putting service to this country before themselves. President Donald Trump has made billions of dollars off his presidency while millions of people are wondering how they’ll afford their health care or how they’ll feed their kids. We’re heading into the most consequential midterm elections of our lifetime, and the stakes are higher than ever before. Fear is contagious, but so is courage, which is why it is critical now more than ever we all do our part and get involved to help elect Democrats nationwide. **That’s why I’m having this conversation with you.** There’s no telling what kind of storm we’re heading into right now. Unfortunately, we need to be prepared for any outcome. **I’ll be answering your questions about what’s ahead for 2026 and how we’re fighting each and every day for Americans.** [**Can you join me on Wednesday, January 21, at 6 PM for this upcoming briefing? America was founded on principles of liberty, personal responsibility, and limited government. Our Constitution was designed to ensure that each generation could enjoy the fruits of freedom without being enslaved by the debts of the past. Yet today, deficit spending--unchecked borrowing by the federal government--threatens to undo this vision. It is not merely poor policy; it is **generational theft** , taking from our children and grandchildren what we cannot sustain ourselves.

Fellow Conservative,

If someone sneaks into our country – or even becomes a citizen – and then brazenly defrauds the American government and hardworking taxpayers out of hundreds of millions of dollars... they should face the ultimate consequence: **deportation after stripping their citizenship.**

Don't you agree that the individuals in Minnesota who ran massive fake child care and food scams – **pocketing over $250 MILLION meant for hungry kids while buying luxury cars, homes, and properties abroad** – deserve to be held fully accountable?

It's outrageous that politicians turned a blind eye while this fraud exploded under weak oversight. Resignations aren't enough – the perpetrators need to face justice to the fullest extent, including _**revoking their naturalized citizenship and sending them back**_ where they came from.

name: Tina Kotek
subject: We will not be divided
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Tina Kotek
body:
Tina for Oregon [https://nvlupin.blob.core.windows.net/images/van/NGP/NGP12/1/92654/images/TinaForOregon-Logo-FullColor-white.png]
Dear Peter,

Like so many Oregonians, I am very concerned about the violent event that unfolded yesterday in a hospital parking lot in Portland’s Hazelwood neighborhood.

Two people were shot and injured by federal agents in our largest city, an unnecessary incident that comes just one day after a tragic death in Minnesota. We all want peace and safety, but this doesn’t get us there.

While details remain limited, one thing is clear: when a president attempts to govern through fear and hate rather than shared values, and endorses policies that tear families apart, he fosters an environment of recklessness and lawlessness.

The priority right now must be a full, complete investigation of the incident, not more detentions that are terrorizing our immigrant communities. The Attorney General, district attorneys, and I have been clear about our concerns with the excessive use of force by federal agents. Yesterday’s events only heighten the urgent need for transparency and accountability. Oregonians deserve clear answers.

Oregonians know how to stand up and speak out peacefully. We must remain united in peaceful opposition to efforts to tear our communities apart and turn us against one another.

We stand united with Minnesota. We stand together as Oregonians. We continue to call for safety in our communities.

With resolve and gratitude,

Tina

PO Box 42307
Portland, OR 97242

subject: We need to impeach Kristi Noem.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Maxine for Congress
body:
https://maxinefororegon.com/ [https://maxinefororegon.com/]
On Wednesday, an ICE officer fired on and killed Renee Nicole Good in cold blood while she was exercising her rights as a legal observer.
Within minutes of the shooting—and without properly investigating the matter—Secretary Noem accused Good of domestic terrorism. This is a baseless accusation, and obviously contradicted by witness statements and video footage.
The day after the killing, another ICE officer shot two people in my district. The Trump administration made it clear that these officers would not be held accountable for illegal actions— even murdering citizens in broad daylight —and now, we’re seeing the consequences.
I am working to bring Articles of Impeachment against Secretary of Homeland Security Kristi Noem to the House floor. Federal officers are not above the law; they should protect and defend the American people, not act with impunity and violence.
If you agree, please add your voice to the petition below: [https://secure.ngpvan.com/06H-VVuO4Eel1yj8wBYuaQ2]
SIGN OUR PETITION [https://secure.ngpvan.com/06H-VVuO4Eel1yj8wBYuaQ2]
We must be assured that a fully transparent investigation is conducted in partnership with Oregon’s Attorney General and local law enforcement. Legitimacy and transparency are critical to earning the public’s trust. Kristi Noem has proven herself to be unserious, unprincipled, and untrustworthy, and she needs to go.
President Donald Trump’s immigration machine is a racist, authoritarian overreach that uses ICE to terrorize our communities. “Might” does not “make right.” Civil liberties are foundational to the success and preservation of our nation.
Americans cannot and should not fear their government. ICE must cease all operations in Portland immediately until they can prove themselves to be trustworthy and bound by the law.
Stay loud,
Maxine

Peter — There’s a lot that has already happened this past year that makes me incredibly angry and upset. But nothing has hit me emotionally like this immigration dragnet. **My grandmother escaped antisemitism in Russia and came through Ellis Island, and that’s a story so many Americans share.** This country is a nation built by immigrants and has always welcomed immigrants, especially those seeking refuge from persecution or discrimination. And people around the world want to come here because we are the land of opportunity. But now, Donald Trump’s militarized ICE agents are violently storming into our neighborhoods to create fear and terror. **The data is clear: they are not targeting convicted criminals – who _should_ be deported – but instead are targeting hard-working, law-abiding friends and neighbors, including many who are pursuing lawful pathways to immigrate here.** Even though the vast majority of immigrants who are arrested are non-violent, masked ICE agents are using excessive violence on the streets of Chicago, New York, New Orleans, and across the country. And just this week, we hit a horrific new low when an overaggressive ICE agent killed an American mother of three in Minneapolis this week — and Donald Trump, Stephen Miller and Kristi Noem immediately concluded that the agent did nothing wrong while excluding state and local law enforcement from investigating. **This lawless behavior has no place in New York, our country, or our democracy.** I’m fighting back against Trump’s anti-immigrant agenda on several fronts. **_First,_ my office in New York became a refuge for immigrant and mixed-status families whose family members were detained by ICE at the neighboring immigration court.** Along with court watchers and advocates, my staff is providing wraparound care to those in need — whether that’s helping families secure their belongings or intervening to deliver “a kick in the ass” when ICE delayed a court-ordered release. [To learn more, check out this excellent [profile](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123002011/594146484/1479585129?refcode=AU_DSG_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260109_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85NDA4NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxNTZiODIxYy1hNmVkLWYwMTEtODE5NC0wMDBkM2ExMWY5MDMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=oKjwzYhW0ZCQKQ1FJJhMSi5tkLjkNv05nAB7zafCzAc=&emci=555bf552-9fed-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&emdi=156b821c-a6ed-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&ceid=13556823).] **_Second,_ I devised and won a lawsuit forcing ICE to allow my colleagues and me to conduct oversight of ICE detention facilities,** which had been ruled by courts to be unconstitutional. Now that I am regularly visiting unannounced, those facilities have been fully cleaned up. **_Third,_ I’ve introduced legislation to prevent ICE from using authoritarian tactics.** More than half of my Democratic colleagues co-sponsor my _**No Secret Police Act**_ , which requires all DHS and ICE agents to remove their masks and clearly display their official identification and badges during civil immigration enforcement operations. I also introduced the **_Immigration Court Due Process Protection Act_** , which prohibits ICE from arresting immigrants showing up for court appearances or mandatory check-ins. And I recently introduced the _**Stop Excessive Force in Immigration Act**_ to ban ICE’s use of crowd control munitions, mandate body cameras, and protect our communities from the abuse of power. **_Finally,_ I demanded that the New York City Police Department enforce city and state laws against ICE agents when they illegally arrest and detain New Yorkers.** This is more important than ever as ICE agents continue to use excessive violence against citizens, like in Minneapolis. **We the people must stand up and fight back.[If you’re with me, please support our campaign with a donation today.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123002012/594146485/-2121819019?amount=10&refcode=AU_DSG_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260109_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85NDA4NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxNTZiODIxYy1hNmVkLWYwMTEtODE5NC0wMDBkM2ExMWY5MDMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=oKjwzYhW0ZCQKQ1FJJhMSi5tkLjkNv05nAB7zafCzAc=)** _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ |

body:

| Hello Forward Friends- Welcome to 2026- year of the midterms! Here at Forward we are thrilled to be able to take all we have learned and achieved over the last couple of election cycles to make really big waves this year across the country and in all levels of government. But of course, we need **YOU**! The first thing we are asking you to do this year is talk about Forward Party with others in your circles. * For volunteers wanting to reach out to their elected officials and introduce them to the party.

We are kicking off this year by recognizing someone who has been an incredible online advocate for our movement from the very beginning, **Michael Leach**! We truly appreciate Michael using his skills to promote our message. He is so talented he was also the winner of our meme contest last summer with Mark Cuban. Thank you, Michael!
Friends, I am truly excited for the year ahead. The political climate in this country has gotten completely out of hand, and I really look forward to helping you spread the message of Forward with your friends and family members so that more people can be a part of this movement to make politics work for the people. I can't wait to see you at an upcoming event!

This week, I filed my 53rd lawsuit against the Trump administration in under a year — this time to stop the illegal freezing of more than $10 billion in childcare funding.
This funding freeze was imposed on five blue states: California, New York, Colorado, Illinois, and Minnesota. There is no evidence to justify targeting California — these funds help low-income families afford child care so parents can work or go to school. To needlessly deprive them of this much-needed support is plain cruel.
I’m suing to block this funding freeze, and I need you on board: if you agree Trump must stop targeting blue states and vulnerable communities with illegal actions, add your name right now. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/tTGw4st-XESsXINLMueppw2]
Look, the American people are sick and tired of President Trump’s lawlessness, lies, and misinformation campaigns.
It is especially pathetic that — once again — his administration’s actions are inflicting harm on the most vulnerable among us.
As a society, we are rightly judged by how we treat our neighbors in need — and this is a shameful way to treat them.
With each passing day, Trump’s “America First” rhetoric is exposed as nothing more than smoke and mirrors.
If he thinks attacking Democratic-led states will silence us, he’s sorely mistaken. California has been fighting back since day one of this presidency, and we’re not stopping anytime soon.

name: Dr. Kristin Hook
subject: ICE must be held accountable
body:
Support Dr. Kristin Hook for Congress in TX-21

| | | | | [|
---](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=3b3aa7dedb&e=395a33a3d2)
| | | | | |
# TGIF.
---
| | It’s been a rough week, hasn’t it?
The President of the United States [kidnapped and imprisoned Venezuela’s leader](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=10a9a89d6c&e=395a33a3d2), likely [breaking international law](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=a7c64db241&e=395a33a3d2) and [setting a dangerous precedent for the world](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=c11e3768db&e=395a33a3d2).
The U.S. marked the five year anniversary of the January 6th insurrection – the first after Trump’s [outrageous pardon of over 1,500 people charged](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=a8b9fbd275&e=395a33a3d2) in the Capitol attack.
And two days ago, [an ICE agent killed a mother](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=56736707bd&e=395a33a3d2) and U.S. citizen in cold blood on the streets of Minneapolis.
---
|
---
|
---
| |

The thing that ties all of these horrific events together is an administration with no guardrails – willing to break the law and then lie about its actions to evade accountability.
DHS Secretary Kristin [Noem claims that the ICE agent was acting in self-defense](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=968e294f63&e=395a33a3d2). But as a scientist with a PhD in animal behavior, what I saw in that video was a predator-prey relationship – Renée Good was trying to get away in her car, and the ICE agent shot her down like prey, ending her life to stop her.
**ICE and Kristi Noem must be held accountable.**
ICE was created under the guise of making our communities safe, but it was done the exact opposite. According to the Marshall Project, [ICE has killed three other people in the last five months](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=519cb4764f&e=395a33a3d2) alone and have threatened others with guns. And yesterday in Portland, [ICE shot and wounded two more people](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=180e29743f&e=395a33a3d2).
Our taxpayer dollars should not be going to a violent terrorist organization.
We are all less safe with violent and masked ICE agents roaming our streets, kidnapping our neighbors, and killing and wounding people.
When I’m elected as a member of Congress, I am fully committed to keeping our communities safe and holding them all accountable.

name: Sophia Bush

body:
I am reaching out about something close to my heart
#

Sophia Bush is an actress and activist who is passionate about making the world a better place. Read this message from Sophia below, then consider [**making a donation to help GIFFORDS PAC stop gun violence in America.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q12026.IDrYd1&refcode=em260109-2-b&t=1&akid=11166%2E3935704%2EkycpgM) Thank you.
* * *

Hi friend,
My name is Sophia Bush. You might be used to seeing me on your TV screen, but today, I am reaching out about an issue that is close to my heart: _Stopping gun violence._
You see it was 2011, and as so many families do, ours had wound up scattered across the country after decades in my mom’s hometown. My first television series would wrap the next year at the end of 2012, and my mom and I had been dreaming about visiting her closest cousin Roxanna and her kids, now in Arizona. One of those “when things slow down a little bit” plans.
**The events of January 8th, 2011 taught my family and me how incredibly unpredictable time is.** How tragically short life can be. My youngest cousin, Christina-Taylor Green, was taken from us before we ever got the chance to visit her. She was shot while waiting in line to meet Gabby Giffords.
At just nine years old, Christina was a leader at her school. She was a dancer and the only girl on her baseball team. She was her big brother Austin’s very best friend. She was just elected to her school’s council and aspired to make the world a better place. She wanted to meet a leader she admired that day.
Yesterday marked 15 years since this terrible tragedy. Every January, I think about my cousin, who never got to grow up to live out her dreams. Who I never knew outside of family email chains and photographs, because we assumed we had more time ahead.
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q12026.IDrYd1&refcode=em260109-2-b&t=2&akid=11166%2E3935704%2EkycpgM)
It can be easy for us to go about our daily lives saying “eventually.” We forget that gun violence is happening around us every day, but for those families affected by it — they can never, ever forget. Their “eventually” never comes.
Unfortunately, gun violence is a uniquely American problem. It is the number one killer of children and young people in our country...but it doesn’t have to be this way.
The work that Gabby Giffords is doing gives me hope. GIFFORDS is working to end our nation’s gun violence crisis by pushing our lawmakers to act — and holding them accountable when they fail to do so.
**[This is not a moment where we can sit back. Will you join me today in standing with Gabby Giffords in her fight to end gun violence in America? We must use our voices to make a change.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q12026.IDrYd1&refcode=em260109-2-b&t=3&akid=11166%2E3935704%2EkycpgM)

clean_body: I am reaching out about something close to my heart Sophia Bush is an actress and activist who is passionate about making the world a better place. Read this message from Sophia below, then consider Thank you. Hi friend, My name is Sophia Bush. You might be used to seeing me on your TV screen, but today, I am reaching out about an issue that is close to my heart: Stopping gun violence. You see it was 2011, and as so many families do, ours had wound up scattered across the country after decades in my mom’s hometown. My first television series would wrap the next year at the end of 2012, and my mom and I had been dreaming about visiting her closest cousin Roxanna and her kids, now in Arizona. One of those “when things slow down a little bit” plans. The events of January 8th, 2011 taught my family and me how incredibly unpredictable time is. How tragically short life can be. My youngest cousin, Christina-Taylor Green, was taken from us before we ever got the chance to visit her. She was shot while waiting in line to meet Gabby Giffords. At just nine years old, Christina was a leader at her school. She was a dancer and the only girl on her baseball team. She was her big brother Austin’s very best friend. She was just elected to her school’s council and aspired to make the world a better place. She wanted to meet a leader she admired that day. Yesterday marked 15 years since this terrible tragedy. Every January, I think about my cousin, who never got to grow up to live out her dreams. Who I never knew outside of family email chains and photographs, because we assumed we had more time ahead. It can be easy for us to go about our daily lives saying “eventually.” We forget that gun violence is happening around us every day, but for those families affected by it — they can never, ever forget. Their “eventually” never comes. Unfortunately, gun violence is a uniquely American problem. It is the number one killer of children and young people in our country...but it doesn’t have to be this way. The work that Gabby Giffords is doing gives me hope. GIFFORDS is working to end our nation’s gun violence crisis by pushing our lawmakers to act — and holding them accountable when they fail to do so. subject: ICE is carrying out violent raids across the country, and they don’t care who gets hurt.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260109-5795-footer&t=1001&akid=5795%2E420207%2EpfuHoW ]Pramila Jayapal

Peter,

We all saw what happened with our own eyes. An American citizen was shot —
not once, not twice. Three times. There are slow-motion videos showing the
reality of this horrific scene all over social media, and yet Trump, JD
Vance, and Kristi Noem are telling lie after lie about ICE’s actions,
trying to wipe this away and undermining trust in our government.

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/51821?c0=pj-email-20260109-1.gfANZv&refcode=em20260109-5795&t=1002&akid=5795%2E420207%2EpfuHoW ][IMG]

ICE is carrying out violent raids across the country — storming workplaces
and neighborhoods, sweeping people off the street, and arresting anyone
they assume doesn’t hold legal status. And Americans are living in fear
that an ICE agent could attack with lethal force at any moment.

They don’t even care who gets hurt:

* ProPublica recently found more than 170 cases this year where American
citizens were detained by ICE agents at raids and protests. And that’s
just what’s been reported.
* And more than 20 U.S. citizens have reported being held for over a day
without being able to call their loved ones or a lawyer. In some
cases, families couldn’t even find them.

And Trump’s cruelty doesn’t stop there. He’s deporting our friends,
co-workers, and neighbors, and now wants to strip naturalized Americans of
their citizenship. It goes against everything this country is supposed to
stand for.

Peter, Trump is
allowing ICE to kidnap U.S. citizens, recklessly use deadly force, and
then lie to cover up their lawlessness.

It’s unacceptable, and the entire administration, including the agents in
question, needs to be held accountable. That means conducting independent
investigations, prosecuting these cases to the full extent of the law, and
cutting funding for the agencies in question until reforms are made.

I know what it means to fight for a place at the table because I’ve lived
it. That’s why I’m relentless about standing up for immigrants, workers,
and families who deserve real representation and real results.

Because this administration’s actions aren’t about community safety. They
aren’t about removing criminals. It’s about targeting immigrant
communities, manufacturing chaos, and tearing families apart to fuel
Trump’s authoritarian agenda.

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-email-20260109-1.lwl9KB&refcode=em20260109-5795&amount=3&t=1003&akid=5795%2E420207%2EpfuHoW ]If you’re with me in demanding accountability, will you pitch in
$3 or whatever you can today to help power this work?

In solidarity,

Pramila Jayapal

subject: Some good news from Washington, D.C.

body:
| | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123003545/594151822/-1072566757?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NDkxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNDRlMDBiYS1hYWVkLWYwMTEtODE5NC0wMDBkM2ExMWY5MDMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=A7_L68QRylfisL05hHzoHcVDFqncK0pIINKps1A6nN0=&emci=206f2d02-84ed-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&emdi=a44e00ba-aaed-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&ceid=21278485)
---
Derek,

As a senior member of the House Armed Services Committee, I have the ability each year to push through important programs and policy changes that keep our nation safe, support our service members, and strengthen our alliances. As you saw from **the video** I released reminding members of the military not to follow illegal orders, our servicemen and women and our national security are priorities of mine. As is holding this administration accountable.
In an ugly, hyperpartisan political climate, it gives me hope that the annual National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) is one area where, although Democrats and Republicans still battle, we ultimately seek compromise for the sake of our country. This most recent NDAA marks the 65th consecutive year that this bill has been signed into law.
Before sharing more – especially given the President’s actions in Venezuela and possible actions elsewhere – I want to make it clear that the NDAA _does not_ give the President or the Pentagon a blank check or permission for their actions. Many of us on the committee oppose the illegal actions in **Venezuela**. Many of us want to help **Ukraine** defend itself against Russia’s aggression. And many agree with me that Defense Secretary **Hegseth** is not just unqualified but reckless and dangerous and should be removed immediately.
Back to the NDAA. There’s a lot in the bill to be proud of – 40 of my priorities are in there – and I want to share some of the highlights with you. These wins are good for our men and women in military and good for Southeast Pennsylvania:
* Sec. Hegseth eliminated the Women’s Initiative Teams (a group identifying and proposing fixes to policies and practices that disproportionately negatively impact women) but I reversed that and made it law.
* President Trump deployed members of the military to U.S. cities and it was often unclear who they were, making oversight difficult and deeply eroding public trust. Going forward, members of the military must have their service clearly visible on their uniform.
* Southeast Pennsylvania is the birthplace of the U.S. helicopter industry and I secured programs that modernize these aircraft while supporting good paying jobs in the region.
* Sec. Hegseth removed staff – including teachers and special education assessors – from military schools across the country. Going forward, he won’t be able to do that. I also secured an expansion of child care services for military families.

These are just a few of the dozens of gains I helped realize in this year’s NDAA. I am incredibly grateful we were able to get this bill over the finish line, Derek. _But with the ongoing unpredictability within the Department of Defense, our work is far from over. _
**We must build on this momentum as we inch closer to the 2026 midterms so we can protect our national security, democracy, and our freedoms. **

The chaos out of Trump’s White House is insanity. | | | [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.SNYHID0cgDJeR88MOfSMuaUOwSMeHgny5jCFLoVuXKaRpYHb0brEongCxHCcly12juOTjGvdZGFN_w9LQ9SOjQ5PFuTRt_tiGVF2MFuOp8SsMKOXMoBOe-ZpnLUVx_FnmtOtLVM_UooWUz2U4lsSzic8RZtVwk10Ea4hMAGpRrgWFHqP9FIErOFs9AB54UnPpIAZjvn0SyXlyuFl6XRJMXEyVzg7BZicAFgHTEESg1U/4n5/XcJVZv4cTNKLIe33KCpl4g/h0/h001.9fV49FeZQ7i3QD3jC_JRtL-sjlrC_Ms2kfDrgkeK5-Q) Friend, On the heels of his attacks in Venezuela, Donald Trump is already talking openly about seizing Greenland by any means necessary, including military force. What timeline are we living in? The chaos out of Trump’s White House is insanity. Americans don’t want more “forever wars.” Even Trump knows this. It’s literally what he ran on. We don’t want more imperialism. And even the people who voted for Trump didn’t vote for him to instigate international conflicts. What this shows us is what many of us have known from the start. Trump ran on the idea of destroying many institutions and checks on power because they allegedly didn’t serve the people. While our institutions certainly do have their flaws, the most important thing they do is provide a check on people like the President. Now, ignoring those checks Trump is using his power not to help the people but to start new wars. This moment demands more than simply taking back the House. It demands a better Democratic Party. We are committed to building that party by directly challenging some of the most complacent and least imaginative members of Congress, those who offer endless explanations for why they cannot confront Trump, but few ideas for what they actually _will_ do. Claiming paralysis because they are in the minority. Yet Republicans have never accepted minority status as an excuse for inaction. We need to build a party of fighters, not folders. To those members of congress who say we can’t do anything I have one message: Retire and pass the torch to someone who is ready to lead in this moment of crisis or be challenged by them. **We’re working to elect a new generation of progressive leaders who will focus on making our lives better and our country stronger, not starting more wars.** **[If you believe in the same future that we do, will you pitch in $5 to power our work? name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
subject: The mistake I made.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
I thought that fascist takeover attempts were going to be architected by evil geniuses.
#
You know, I made a mistake early on:
From all the movies that we see growing up about heroes and villains, I thought that fascist takeover attempts were going to be architected by evil _geniuses._
I was not expecting how unearned, nepotistic, mediocre, and just dumb so many of the people architecting this were going to be and it works because of brute force.
You can do anything through brute force, but it's not sophisticated and it does not merit our intellectual respect.
**That's my thought of the day.**
And even to that, that's why the right says: “you were a bartender, you were a bartender” to kind of project their insecurities onto me, but, I did something. I ran for Congress and won because of the incredible support from my neighbors.
Republicans want us to resign ourselves to cynicism but giving up is a privilege we can’t afford. Through solidarity we can make a new world, a better country, where our work has dignity and our lives have respect.
I can’t do this work without you — the grassroots supporters who have had my back every step of the way. I don't curry favor with billionaires or host exclusive fundraising events. This campaign's average donation floats around $17-20.
Together, we’ve built a movement that won’t back down. Thank you for being a part of it.

_**by Lawrence Winnerman, COO**_
We are being asked--implicitly, aggressively, whether we consent or not--to choose our martyrs.
That alone should terrify you.
But if we are living in a country where people feel compelled to declare _which dead American they stand with_ , if we are sliding into some dystopian moral Hunger Games where allegiance is expressed through slogans and bodies, then I want to be perfectly clear:
**I am Renee Good.**
Not because martyrdom is noble. Not because death should ever be the price of citizenship. But because if this country is going to demand that we choose who represents "real America," then the choice should not even be close.
Charlie Kirk represents a nightmare vision of this country.
Renee Good represents its fragile, endangered soul.
_Charlie Kirk was not an American patriot._ He was a professional arsonist of the civic fabric--someone who built a career on fake outrage, bad-faith argument, and the systematic erosion of the American promise. He made millions telling people that their neighbors were enemies, that cruelty was strength, that fear was wisdom, and that democracy itself was something to sneer at if it failed to produce the outcomes he wanted.
Renee Good was a queer mother of three. A poet. A neighbor. A human being who cared about her community and the people in it--especially the ones with less power, less safety, and fewer voices.
She lived compassion in a way that didn't require a microphone or a donor list. And that compassion is almost certainly what put her in the path of federal agents who never should have been there, doing a job they were wildly unqualified to do.
She did not die because she was reckless.
She did not die because she was violent.
She did not die because she was dangerous.
She died because she cared.
She died because she believed that warning her neighbors--her fellow Minneapolis residents--that ICE was conducting raids was the right thing to do. Because she believed community mattered. Because she believed people deserved to know when armed agents of the federal government were sweeping through their lives.
* * *
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.SGZLyWIdLsag9kmxV7ykHIQXfQrqrFE67ElZgUpkWns?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=184068910)
* * *
And for that--for what at worst amounts to a trivial vehicle or parking issue, for trying to move her car, for trying to comply--she was shot in the face in front of her partner, after dropping her child off at daycare.
That is not law enforcement.
That is not protection.
That is not America.
Let's dispense with the official lies immediately.
The narrative coming out of the Department of Homeland Security and the White House is bullshit. It collapses under even the slightest moral or factual pressure. Renee Good did nothing to deserve harassment, intimidation, or death. The ICE officers involved did not de-escalate. They did not protect. They did not help. They panicked. They reacted to a minor, solvable situation with lethal force.
And then they prevented help from reaching her as she lay dying by the side of the road.
That is not a tragic accident.
That is a systemic failure.
One of the stated duties of ICE is to help and protect. They did neither. Instead, they proved something we have been refusing to face: we have armed the least prepared, least accountable, least morally serious people with extraordinary power over life and death.
And they are using it.
Renee Good is not an anomaly. She is a warning.
We are in a battle for the soul of this country. Renee Good is among the first people dying in the open--not in some distant war zone, not under a foreign flag, but here, at home, in broad daylight.
* * *
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=184068910&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg0MDY4OTEwLCJpYXQiOjE3Njc5OTg5NjYsImV4cCI6MTc3MDU5MDk2NiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.SS7SOvF7FxHHMvPFE_HzOWu1_-qDd8LUyR752NiJcYg)
* * *
This is what the early stages of authoritarianism look like. It is not tanks in the streets, or dramatic declarations. It is normalization. Bureaucracy. Federal agents operating with impunity. Official statements that insult our intelligence. And a steady drumbeat of "justified" violence against people who were never threats to begin with.
What is coming--what will be required of Americans who want to reclaim the soul of this country--is not going to be comfortable. It is not going to look like flag pins and slogans and nostalgic speeches about a past that never quite existed.
It is going to look much closer to what Renee Good experienced.
It is going to involve risk.
It is going to involve standing up when it's inconvenient.
It is going to involve protecting people the state has decided are expendable.
For decades, white middle-class America has been insulated from this reality. We have told ourselves that brutality is something that happens "over there," to "other people," in communities we don't have to think about too hard. Renee Good shatters that illusion.
She was one of us.
She was _America_.
And that is precisely why she is dangerous to the Charlie Kirk vision of this country.
Because Charlie Kirk's America requires fear. It requires enemies. It requires a population so divided, so suspicious of one another, that they will cheer when the state crushes the "right" people, the ones they hate.
Charlie Kirk's America is hierarchical, cruel, and deeply comfortable with violence--as long as it's justified by ideology and aimed downward.
Renee Good's America is the opposite.
Her America is communal. It is empathetic. It assumes shared responsibility. It believes that citizenship means looking out for one another, and not turning neighbors into targets. Her life, and her death, expose just how hollow the other vision really is.
* * *
[Leave a comment](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=184068910&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&isFreemail=true&comments=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg0MDY4OTEwLCJpYXQiOjE3Njc5OTg5NjYsImV4cCI6MTc3MDU5MDk2NiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.SS7SOvF7FxHHMvPFE_HzOWu1_-qDd8LUyR752NiJcYg&r=1hvr60&utm_campaign=email-half-magic-comments&action=post-comment)
* * *
If you find yourself wanting to declare "I am Charlie Kirk," you should ask yourself what that actually means.
It means you are choosing power over people.
It means you are choosing cruelty over care.
It means you are choosing a vision of America where the machinery of the state is more sacred than human life.
That is not patriotism--it is submission to the iron fist of authoritarianism.
Real patriotism is refusing to accept a country where kindness is punished with a bullet. Real patriotism is saying no--loudly, publicly, and repeatedly--to federal violence carried out in our name. Real patriotism is honoring people like Renee Good not as symbols, but as standards.
If we must choose, then choose the person who lived their values without profit. Choose the person who showed up for their community without applause. Choose the person whose instinct, when faced with injustice, was to warn, to protect, to care.
**Choose Renee Good.**
Say her name not as a slogan, but as a commitment.
Because the nightmare America that killed her is already here--and the only way it doesn't win is if we decide, collectively, that we will no longer tolerate it.
**I am Renee Good.**
And if you still believe in the promise of this country, you should be too.

clean_body: It’s a damn shame. | | = Hi team, Yesterday, House Democrats and Republicans came together to pass the Breaking the Gridlock Act and extend the ACA subsidies that expired this month. Our congressman, Dan Meuser, voted no – and threw thousands of people in his district under the bus. He voted AGAINST stopping the huge premium increases that many across our district have seen. He voted not to save coverage for the families that lost it. It’s a damn shame! There are 1,000 Pennsylvanians a day dropping their health insurance because they can’t pay the bill. People here deserve access to affordable coverage. And our hospitals and health clinics – and the countless people they employ – depend on it. Dan Meuser would rather force his constituents to choose between seeing a doctor and feeding their family than show an ounce of bipartisanship. He literally voted to keep the gridlock. And we’re the ones paying the price. If you recently lost your insurance or you're struggling with rising costs like so many of our neighbors here in PA-09, don’t donate. | Our team is doing everything we can to reverse this dangerous course.
# [](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/61?t=1&akid=9396%2E5257348%2Er7Zk2L)
Derek – The president’s ongoing attacks on the press and free speech are putting our First Amendment rights in grave danger.
For the first time in a generation, we have censorship of the press.
Not because the government prohibits the publication of offending material.
But because the administration coerces and dangles corrupt incentives like help with billion-dollar mergers.
And large corporations with media holdings have decided to self-censor to appease a wannabe dictator.
This is how democracies die.
Most recently, _CBS News_ pulled a 60 Minutes segment on Trump deportations — preemptively trying not to anger the President while their parent company tries to purchase Warner Bros. Earlier this year, my friend Jimmy Kimmel’s show was pulled from the air, only to be restored when the public outcry became too great. The Trump administration has gone after the _New York Times_ , _Wall Street Journal_ , and other outlets.
This is dangerous — and we need to do everything we can to reverse this dangerous course and work toward making free speech the norm, not the exception. **[If you can, will you donate $10 to help us protect freedom of speech and fight back against this wannabe dictator?](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1312?c0=q12026_abs_em.khhTGf&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_GEN_GEN_AC90_20260109_PM1_V1_S1&t=4&akid=9396%2E5257348%2Er7Zk2L)**

name: Team Fetterman
subject: everyone has an opinion about AI – we want yours
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Fetterman for PA
body:
[ https://act.johnfetterman.com/go/51612?refcode=jtk402-su-fl-header&t=1001&akid=10528%2E434096%2EVXLiEF ]John Fetterman

Folks, data centers to power AI are popping up around the country, especially in places with a lot of water nearby – like our Great Lakes.

Some folks are embracing these changes, others are concerned about the environmental impacts and potential electric bill hikes.

The thing is ... the genie might be out of the bottle when it comes to AI. It's here, and it's not going away. If that's the case:

1️⃣ We should use it for good things,
2️⃣ We definitely can't let billionaires run with it, and
3️⃣ Companies should pay for the energy they use.

John's already working to make sure AI is used responsibly. Right before the holidays, he introduced a bipartisan bill to help academic and industry researchers share and process information. It'll help our country innovate and move faster – that's how we compete.

But John knows we can't let Big Tech run wild. No one gets a blank check.

Axios reported that the CEO of a self-driving truck company REJECTED Teamsters' demand for human operators. Not on our watch. 🙅

John stands with the Teamsters. We can't have robots replacing good union jobs, especially when public safety is at risk. These rigs should always have a trained professional in the cab. Roads are not a tech experiment.

There's a balance – so we're digging into this. And John needs to hear from you. Will you take 60 seconds to share your thoughts on AI by clicking this link or the button below?

https://act.johnfetterman.com/go/52527?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&t=1002&akid=10528%2E434096%2EVXLiEF

Thanks for weighing in,

Team Fetterman 💛

name: Mark Kelly
subject: Hegseth’s threats
body:
You swear an oath to the Constitution when you join the military — including the First Amendment right to free speech. We swore to defend the foundational principles of this country. I took that oath seriously 40 years ago, and I still do.
#
Team,
Pete Hegseth decided he's going to censure me, and is threatening to demote me and reduce my pension.
I got shot at in service to this country. I missed holidays and birthdays. I commanded a space shuttle mission and launched to the International Space Station while my wife recovered from a gunshot wound to the head.
My rank and retirement are things that I earned through my service and sacrifice for this country. Generations of servicemembers have done the same. Pete Hegseth wants to send a message to every single one that he will come after them if they say something he doesn’t like.
You swear an oath to the Constitution when you join the military — including the First Amendment right to free speech. We swore to defend the foundational principles of this country. I took that oath seriously 40 years ago, and I still do.
Pete Hegseth can threaten to reduce my rank and my pension. But I am not going to let him intimidate me, or anyone else. He is not going to stop me from defending our democracy from a president who is hellbent on destroying it.
If they think this is going to shut me up, they’ve got another thing coming.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123004482/594155307/1575317576?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82NzYzNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlM2JlYjU4OS1hZmVkLWYwMTEtODE5NC0wMDBkM2ExMWY5MDMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogIkRQV0lMTElTNjdAR01BSUwuQ09NIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=FlnrMFJ5OnhgtyRJRk8TMQVhPt_GR2hnpsGQYjtv37Q=&emci=96bf4a8c-a3ed-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&emdi=e3beb589-afed-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&ceid=4925535) Leaders at INDOT this week announced that over 300 road projects all over Indiana are being canceled because the funds are not there. However, at the same time, the state is preparing for vast reserves well above the expected amount when the budget was passed in the Spring of 2025. One of the projects still moving forawrd is the Mid-States Corridor project which would connect Jasper to I-69. The project's $1 billion price tag is no problem, seemingly because it will help out Governor Braun's own distribution company. Braun has proven to only be looking out for himself throughout his first year in charge, and this is just the latest example. He's cancelling over 300 projects important to your communities in order to pay for his company road. It's time for him to do the right thing, and tell INDOT to fund other important projects before paying for this single road. On top of it, Braun's administration has confirmed it has asked the federal government for permission to toll Interstate 70 from Terre Haute to Richmond. ****_Each week, the State Party will highlight key policy from Democrats at the Statehouse or across the state. Democrats deliver a better future for Hoosier families, and we urge you to share this information with your networks._ [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123004483/594155308/1664554166?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82NzYzNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlM2JlYjU4OS1hZmVkLWYwMTEtODE5NC0wMDBkM2ExMWY5MDMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogIkRQV0lMTElTNjdAR01BSUwuQ09NIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=FlnrMFJ5OnhgtyRJRk8TMQVhPt_GR2hnpsGQYjtv37Q=&emci=96bf4a8c-a3ed-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&emdi=e3beb589-afed-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&ceid=4925535) Last night, Indiana Democratic U.S. Reps. Frank Mrvan and André Carson joined every Democratic member of Congress in voting to extend the enhanced ACA premium tax credits that Republicans let expire by passing the Big Bad Bill in 2025. The result of those credits expiring has been awful for Hoosier families. Over 300,000 Hoosiers saw their yearly premiums double or even triple due to the expiring of the credits. Reps. Mrvan and Carson have been working hard to reinstate these credits and make sure every Hoosier can afford healthcare. 17 Republicans joined in every Democrat in voting to extend the credits, meaning it did pass the House. These Republicans heard from their residents facing these steep increases, and finally did the right thing. However, not a single one of Indiana's seven congressional Republicans voted in favor of these credits. [INDems called on Indiana's GOP members to support these credits on Thursday, but none of them did.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123004484/594155309/-568900257?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82NzYzNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlM2JlYjU4OS1hZmVkLWYwMTEtODE5NC0wMDBkM2ExMWY5MDMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogIkRQV0lMTElTNjdAR01BSUwuQ09NIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=FlnrMFJ5OnhgtyRJRk8TMQVhPt_GR2hnpsGQYjtv37Q=&emci=96bf4a8c-a3ed-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&emdi=e3beb589-afed-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&ceid=4925535) That's a slap in the face to hardworking Hoosiers who are just trying to afford their healthcare. If you opened this, I'm grateful. We all get too many emails. So, in 2026, I want to sharpen my focus on quality over quantity. I'm going to send you fewer emails this year; in fact, as few as possible. And I want them to accomplish more. (As the year goes on, feel free to use replies in the Notes feature on Substack to give me feedback on what you're seeing here.)
Specifically, I want to do two things:
* _**One, provide something like the insight or "texture" people get when they're close to campaigns**_, as way of helping our community of readers find good ways to take action. You don't need another commentator on the news. I'll try to show you, through occasional interviews with candidates and other difference-makers, what's happening on the ground. This could help you decide what and who are worthy of your time and investment. With the same goal, I'll share accounts of my own travels.
* _**Two, send you exactly what I 'm saying in places you might not be**_. I want to get back to the discipline of writing speeches. There has been a lot said lately about the effect of reading and writing on thought, and what we risk losing as everything becomes short-form video. We should keep asking our politicians to give speeches that sound like someone took the time to think about them ahead of time. (An actual person.) So, I'm going to do a better job writing them myself.

Last: a great number of you responded to my request for help for the Trade Institute of Pittsburgh on Giving Tuesday. It made a real difference. Thank you for your generosity!

U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Montgomery) is calling out the dangerous and irresponsible rhetoric coming from leaders in the Democratic Party after a woman was killed in Minneapolis by an ICE officer acting in self defense.

According to the Department of Homeland Security, Renee Nicole Good was shot and killed by an ICE agent after she allegedly tried using her vehicle as a weapon. Latest reports indicate Good was “stalking and impeding” ICE agents throughout the day of the incident.

Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey accused the agent of committing murder and said ICE needs to leave the city.

Britt discussed the situation Thursday on Newsmax.

“Well, first and foremost, this is a tragic situation,” Britt said. “As you said yourself, any loss of life is something that we all mourn when we look at where we are and how we got here. The left has to assume responsibility for creating an environment that should have never existed.”

The past year has certainly been a memorable one – and, more importantly, a rewarding one.

Beginning the year by leading the Laken Riley Act through the Senate and to President Trump’s desk – and seeing it become the first bill he signed into law in his second term –was just the start of what we have accomplished for Alabamians and Americans alike. Trump and Republicans campaigned on cracking down on illegal migration, and this legislation sent an immediate and unmistakable message to the nation that we intended to keep that promise.

Since then, border crossings have reached historic lows, resulting in countless lives saved. Whether it’s stopping deadly fentanyl or violent criminals from crossing our border, the success in securing our nation is undeniable.

Friends,
Thanks to God, Judge Estudillo, and all of you, **my husband has been home since December 22nd**. We've spent the last couple of weeks doing two things at once: recovering from a household flu (solidarity to everyone in the winter virus trenches), and quietly absorbing the miracle of having the soul of my soul back under our roof again--present with the kids, present in our kitchen, present in the small, sacred ordinariness that was stolen from us for far too long.
And we've also done something else--something strategic, stabilizing, and long overdue:
We created a **single source of legal truth** for this entire 25-year saga.
Here it is: **[The Full Saga, for the Ninth Circuit](https://substack.com/redirect/1b099867-fd04-4e55-9042-37153ee8540a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
And here are the supporting exhibits: **[Chaudhry-NinthCircuit-Exhibits Folder](https://substack.com/redirect/1b099867-fd04-4e55-9042-37153ee8540a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
This post is the short, summarized human version of that record: the story arc in plain language with no fluff--so you can understand what happened, why it matters, and what the Ninth Circuit now has the power to do.
* * *
## The saga, in one continuous line
### 1) He came to America in the 1990s -- and built a life here
Zahid arrived in the United States in the '90s. He worked, paid taxes, built community, and became, in every meaningful way, an American--long before anyone was willing to admit it on paper.
### 2) He joined the U.S. military _before_ 9/11
This matters legally. It matters morally. And it matters historically.
Because veterans who served in designated periods are eligible for **expedited naturalization pathways** that Congress created explicitly to honor service and sacrifice. In Zahid's case, the timeline is especially clear: he served, he was eligible, and by the early 2000s--around **2002** --his citizenship should have been routine.
It wasn't.
### 3) After 9/11, he was aggressively pressured to do things he believed were unconstitutional
What happened next is the kind of story Americans still struggle to believe about our own government--until it happens to someone they love.
In the post-9/11 climate, Zahid was pressured toward actions and roles that, in his view, crossed ethical and constitutional lines. They wanted him to spy for them. They wanted him to just "give a name" \- someone who would be framed and smeared as a "terrorist," who would have their life destroyed so those who'd recruited him could get their promotions. Zahid was offered an easy life, six-figure-plus pay, comfortable work, desk job, citizenship, all the perks. He refused--quietly, firmly, as a matter of principle.
And he was punished for it.
### 4) "We'll make your life hell" -- and the "agency interest" flag
We now have sworn testimony that an agent explicitly said they would place an **" agency interest" flag** in his file so **USCIS would never naturalize him**.
That alleged statement is not a metaphor. It is not a dramatic flourish. It is the kind of "administrative shadow" that can follow someone for decades--silently contaminating every process, every application, every chance at normal life.
Then, as if that wasn't enough, he and Ann were targeted, followed, harassed, called aggressively at 3am, approached by strangers in the grocery store, staked out in their own neighborhoods, over and over again. Friends told them about agents asking about them, pressuring them, threatening their jobs. They lost people over it. And remember - they did _nothing wrong_.
If you've ever wondered how a person can do everything right and still be trapped indefinitely inside a bureaucracy: this is how.
### 5) He was routed into CARRP -- the black box
Zahid's case bears the markers of **CARRP** -style treatment: opaque, national-security-coded delays and denials; shifting rationales; innuendo substituted for evidence; and a system that is almost impossible to challenge from the outside because it hides behind secrecy and deference.
CARRP is the "Extreme Vetting" program that USCIS asked Congress for permission to do _eleven times_ , and Congress refused. CARRP **is not law**. Only Congress can make immigration law. But CARRP has functionally shadow-banned and often deported tens of thousands of law-abiding aspiring Americans who did everything right. The affected person is never told what the "concerns" are - there's no chance to face your accuser, respond to the accusations, defend yourself in court, none of that. The only way we know for sure that Zahid was CARRP'd is from documents it took a FOIA request to find.
In the legal filings, you'll see that we lay out what we can prove, what we can reasonably infer, and what the record strongly supports. The overall pattern is unmistakable--**a legal life slowed, distorted, and obstructed by something deeper and far more malicious than "normal processing."**
### 6) A pretextual "final order of removal," full of lies and misrepresentations
For years, Zahid was treated--publicly and administratively--as if he had some settled, unquestionable "final order of removal."
But the record shows that label was used in ways that were inaccurate, exaggerated, and, at times, flatly false (and later contradicted by sworn testimony). We have the receipts.
This "order" became a kind of administrative cudgel: a phrase that was repeated over and over in an attempt to give it the weight of inevitability, even when it did not match reality.
### 7) Seventeen years of litigation -- because there was no other way to survive
For the past **17 years** , Zahid fought this through the courts because the normal channels did not correct themselves. They escalated.
This is what people don't grasp until they live it: when an administrative machine decides you are "problematic," the process is not merely slow--it becomes adversarial, punitive, and existential. And it consumes tens of thousands of hours of your life.
### 8) The wrongful detention -- and the judge's line that still echoes
And then came the detention that brought everything to a head.
Zahid was unlawfully detained in a way that shocked even the federal judge who ultimately ordered his release. The judge's written order included a line that should chill anyone who believes in basic due process and the rule of law:
**" Where were the lawyers?"**
That is not the language of routine disagreement. That is judicial alarm.
### 9) Now: the entire saga is before the Ninth Circuit
At long last, the full record is in front of the **Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals**.
And the stakes are enormous.
The Ninth Circuit has the power--if it chooses--to end this whole thing decisively, including:
* **Backdated naturalization** (which matters not only for dignity and restoration, but also because it would open the door for Zahid to **run for office** if he chooses), and
* **Damages and accountability** where the law supports them.

That would not be "special treatment." It would be the opposite: the restoration of what should have happened decades ago, and the recognition of what was done instead.
Or, they could side with the ones who've abused my husband's dignity, integrity, service, and sacrifice for twenty-five years.
There's a line in a poem I wrote while he was inside:
> "And though his nation may not yet deserve his loyalty,
> I will not let it dishonor his soul."
* * *
There are sickening details sprinkled throughout all of this, but let me highlight just a few:
* After Zahid's abduction, someone hacked Google Search results so that the _first_ _result_ when you searched for his name was the baseless and nauseating allegation that he raped an underage girl. It's a baldfaced lie. I have the screenshot. (You can read my account about it [here](https://substack.com/redirect/c2d6067e-bce0-4022-8bf5-c104adab402f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), page 7-10. And about the neighbor who asked me if Zahid married me when I was 13...page 11.)
* At the weaponized citizenship appointment, the man who interviewed Zahid -- who refused to give his name, and refused even to write his name _on the official paperwork_ , a major due-process failure that means we have no idea who that was, or who he even worked for -- asserted, out of the blue, that Zahid owed the VA almost half a million dollars in "overpaid compensation."
That's bullshit. My husband is wheelchair-bound, constantly in pain, and requires complex medical care due to disabling injuries he sustained on active-duty service, and he already gets _much_ _less_ than many veterans with far less severe disabilities. Now they're telling him he has to pay back half a million dollars or they'll cut off his benefits, which we depend on, _starting next month_.
* The first Zahid _ever_ heard of this supposed debt, was at that interview, from this anonymous officer. ICE grabbed him moments later.
* BUT, somehow, that same accusation made it into the DHS smear that was widely publicized about him, less than two weeks later.
* ONLY AFTER THAT, did our family receive a formal letter from the VA informing us of this supposed debt - still with no explanation. That notification letter was dated September 26, 2025...over a month after he'd been taken.
* The evidence is in [this document](https://substack.com/redirect/d2a0b24a-84a6-4bda-826a-8d2a48734718?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Make it make sense.
* When they issued Zahid's "final order of removal," the key claim was that he "falsely claimed citizenship" on a Yakima police reserve volunteer application in the early '00s, before his injuries. First, it was a volunteer position, it doesn't even matter. Second, he _didn 't_ claim citizenship, he **left that box blank**. Later, the box came back from the reviewer with a _check mark_ , like the check marks next to all the other questions and next to his references -- not the neat "X" Zahid used to mark all the other boxes. But, that officer who reviewed Zahid's application took it to the FBI to lie that Zahid "falsely claimed citizenship."
Too bad that he also bragged to the leader of the local militia that he was 'going to get several promotions framing Zahid as a terrorist.' And he was also proud to make overtly racist comments in public places, while in uniform... creating a clear and proven pattern of bias.
As soon as it was discovered that Zahid was going to call that militia leader as a witness, bam, his trial was canceled (it had been planned for a year, and was supposed to be a full week long) and the old Yakima judge rubber-stamped the accusations against Zahid, which baked them into the legal record without _ever_ being tested in court. That case, _Chaudhry v. Napolitano_ , is _still_ weaponized against Zahid by the same people who lied, smeared, and targeted him this whole time. (It was quoted in the DHS hit piece on September 4th, 2025. For crying out loud.)
That officer... when Zahid finally got him under oath, _he freely admitted that Zahid never claimed citizenship_. This was back in 2010! Yet **STILL** , every time they say "Zahid has a final order of removal," they are directly invoking this **one man 's proven lie** that Zahid "claimed citizenship" by checking a box he never checked, on a form where it didn't matter anyway, when all he was trying to do was, AGAIN, serve his community selflessly and honestly as best he could.
There's a whole section on this stuff. Starts on [page 47](https://substack.com/redirect/58d59dfa-de69-4bd0-a989-612e34dfd5f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

> _And if you 'd prefer to read the non-legalese version, give me a minute. _
> _The book is coming next._
* * *
## Why this matters beyond our family
This story is about Zahid--but it's also about what happens when:
* **principled refusal** is treated as a threat,
* **bureaucratic secrecy** becomes unreviewable power, and
* a person can be functionally exiled from full belonging--**not because of what they did** , but because of what they refused to do.

If our institutions can do this to a veteran who served this country, they can do it to anyone.
And they often do.
* * *
## What you can do right now
1. **Read the single source of legal truth** (if you have the bandwidth for it):
[Ninth Circuit: Petitioner's Supplemental Memorandum, Case No. 21-1160](https://substack.com/redirect/58d59dfa-de69-4bd0-a989-612e34dfd5f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
2. **Browse the exhibits** (if you want receipts, not rhetoric):
[Ninth Circuit: Exhibits Folder](https://substack.com/redirect/1b099867-fd04-4e55-9042-37153ee8540a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
3. **Share this post** with one sentence you believe in.
Not twenty paragraphs. One sentence. Something like:

* "A U.S. veteran fought 25 years for citizenship after refusing unconstitutional pressure."
* "Due process is not optional--especially for the people we send to war."
* "This is what administrative punishment looks like."

* * *
## A personal note, because we're human
We've had the flu. The house has been a chorus of coughs and tea cups and children's Tylenol and crumpled tissues. And in the middle of it, I keep catching myself watching Zahid do utterly normal things--washing dishes, cuddling a sleeping child, laughing at something on the internet--and feeling this almost unbearable relief.
Home is not abstract. Home is medicine.
**Thank you** to everyone who stood with us when it wasn't safe, when it wasn't convenient, when it wasn't popular. Thank you for your prayers, your encouragement, your support, your witness, your refusal to look away.
Now we wait for the Ninth Circuit--with clarity, with patience, with each other, and with our spine intact.
**More soon.**
--Melissa

My husband is wheelchair-bound, constantly in pain, and requires complex medical care due to disabling injuries he sustained on active-duty service, and he already gets much less than many veterans with far less severe disabilities. Now they're telling him he has to pay back half a million dollars or they'll cut off his benefits, which we depend on, starting next month. The first Zahid ever heard of this supposed debt, was at that interview, from this anonymous officer. ICE grabbed him moments later. BUT, somehow, that same accusation made it into the DHS smear that was widely publicized about him, less than two weeks later. ONLY AFTER THAT, did our family receive a formal letter from the VA informing us of this supposed debt - still with no explanation. That notification letter was dated September 26, 2025...over a month after he'd been taken. The evidence is in . Make it make sense. When they issued Zahid's "final order of removal," the key claim was that he "falsely claimed citizenship" on a Yakima police reserve volunteer application in the early '00s, before his injuries. First, it was a volunteer position, it doesn't even matter. Second, he didn 't claim citizenship, he left that box blank. Later, the box came back from the reviewer with a check mark , like the check marks next to all the other questions and next to his references -- not the neat "X" Zahid used to mark all the other boxes. But, that officer who reviewed Zahid's application took it to the FBI to lie that Zahid "falsely claimed citizenship." Too bad that he also bragged to the leader of the local militia that he was 'going to get several promotions framing Zahid as a terrorist.' And he was also proud to make overtly racist comments in public places, while in uniform... creating a clear and proven pattern of bias. As soon as it was discovered that Zahid was going to call that militia leader as a witness, bam, his trial was canceled (it had been planned for a year, and was supposed to be a full week long) and the old Yakima judge rubber-stamped the accusations against Zahid, which baked them into the legal record without ever being tested in court. That case, Chaudhry v. Napolitano , is still weaponized against Zahid by the same people who lied, smeared, and targeted him this whole time. (It was quoted in the DHS hit piece on September 4th, 2025. For crying out loud.) That officer... when Zahid finally got him under oath, he freely admitted that Zahid never claimed citizenship. This was back in 2010! Yet STILL , every time they say "Zahid has a final order of removal," they are directly invoking this one man 's proven lie that Zahid "claimed citizenship" by checking a box he never checked, on a form where it didn't matter anyway, when all he was trying to do was, AGAIN, serve his community selflessly and honestly as best he could. There's a whole section on this stuff. Starts on . And if you 'd prefer to read the non-legalese version, give me a minute. The book is coming next. Why this matters beyond our family This story is about Zahid--but it's also about what happens when: principled refusal is treated as a threat, bureaucratic secrecy becomes unreviewable power, and a person can be functionally exiled from full belonging--not because of what they did , but because of what they refused to do. If our institutions can do this to a veteran who served this country, they can do it to anyone. And they often do. What you can do right now 1. Read the single source of legal truth (if you have the bandwidth for it): 2. Browse the exhibits (if you want receipts, not rhetoric): 3. Share this post with one sentence you believe in. Not twenty paragraphs. One sentence. Something like: "A U.S. veteran fought 25 years for citizenship after refusing unconstitutional pressure." "Due process is not optional--especially for the people we send to war." "This is what administrative punishment looks like." A personal note, because we're human We've had the flu. The house has been a chorus of coughs and tea cups and children's Tylenol and crumpled tissues. And in the middle of it, I keep catching myself watching Zahid do utterly normal things--washing dishes, cuddling a sleeping child, laughing at something on the internet--and feeling this almost unbearable relief. Home is not abstract. Home is medicine. Thank you to everyone who stood with us when it wasn't safe, when it wasn't convenient, when it wasn't popular. Thank you for your prayers, your encouragement, your support, your witness, your refusal to look away. Now we wait for the Ninth Circuit--with clarity, with patience, with each other, and with our spine intact. More soon. --Melissa | | ---|---|--- You 're currently a free subscriber to "It's a Matter of Integrity" by Melissa Chaudhry.
